Subject: Commissioning playbook for Reserved fleet onboarding - ACME-4572

Samira —

Following up from yesterday's kickoff: attached is a concise commissioning playbook tailored to the ACME-4572 reserved capacity purchase. This is focused on the hosted->reserved commissioning sequence we discussed: capacity verification, performance acceptance, and the production cutover window. High-level ask: please review the acceptance gates and confirm the preferred 2-hour cutover window in the week of Mar 21.

What this email contains (attachments + short summary):
- Preflight checklist (attachment: reserved-fleet-commissioning-checklist.pdf) — items we need ACME signoff on before we provision reserved instances.
- Preflight load script (attachment: preflight-loadscript.json) — quick reproducible traffic profile for throughput/latency acceptance.
- SLA gating matrix (attachment: sla-gating-matrix.xlsx) — pass/fail criteria for go/no-go.

Key timeline (proposed):
- Mar 15: Provision reserved pool + smoke boot (internal)
- Mar 16–17: Preflight validation (ACME and Redwood joint testing)
- Mar 18: Capacity verification report + final acceptance
- Mar 21: Planned cutover (2-hour maintenance window) with fallback to hosted API for 30 minutes following cutover

Acceptance criteria highlights (short):
- 95th percentile latency within 20% of hosted baseline for <512 token completions.
- Throughput sustaining 2.5x peak RPS observed last month for 30 minutes.
- No functional regressions observed in the model outputs for held prompt set.

Ben & Grace — I'm looping you for commercial/CS coordination and to own the DocuSign/PO steps.

Samira — if that timeline looks tight, tell us which dates in the window work best and we'll adapt.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserved-fleet-commissioning-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48 KB); preflight-loadscript.json (JSON, 6 KB); sla-gating-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 22 KB)

Thanks for the pickup. Quick answers inline and an updated plan below. I've also attached the security appendix and a short runbook snippet for the preflight tests.

- Mar 15 (EOD): PO submitted by ACME (contracts@acmecorp.com)
- Mar 16: Reserved pool provisioned (internal smoke)

Acceptance gates (updated):
- Latency: p95 < 1.25x hosted baseline for <512 tokens (we tightened the margin)
- Throughput: sustain target RPS for 30 mins with <1% error budget consumption
- Output quality: no more than 1% token-level divergence on held prompt set

Samira / ACME team —

Quick engineering confirmation from Redwood:

Preflight outputs we will deliver in the report (structured, machine-readable + PDF):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency histograms by token-length bucket
- per-model throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, and sustained RPS windows
- KV-cache hit/miss stats and prefix cache efficiency
- model hash/version + tokenizer fingerprint for reproducibility
- sample output diffs for the held prompt set (human-review table + token-divergence rate)

Telemetry delivery: we will push a compressed JSON report to the ACME Drive folder and a flattened CSV into the Splunk HTTP ingest endpoint you shared. During the post-cutover monitoring window we will also stream a reduced telemetry set to the monitoring channel (latency p95, error rate, token counts) every 60s.

Go/no-go checklist (brief):
- All critical tests pass in preflight (latency gating, throughput hold run)
- No data-plane errors > 0.5% for 30 minutes
- Confirmed network path and firewall rules from ACME partner (Andrew)

We are set to run the joint preflight on Mar 16 at 09:00 PT; please reply if you need a different anchor time.

Karthik
